info.name: Board Game Platform — backend :3000
info.description:
The public REST surface of `backend/`, as it stands at the end of **Phase E (S21–S22)**.

## Import and run

1. Import this file **and** an environment: `Template.local.postman_environment.json` (port 3000, the normal one) or `Template.local-3999.postman_environment.json` (fallback). Then **select it in the environment dropdown, top right** — an unselected environment is the single most common reason this collection appears broken.
2. Start the API: `cd backend && npm run db:reset && npm run dev`.
3. **Run the whole collection in order** (Collection Runner), or click through the folders top to bottom. Requests capture ids into collection variables for the ones that follow, so order matters.

Every request carries assertions, so a collection run is a real smoke test: 0 failures means the surface behaves. It is *not* a replacement for `npm test` — the vitest suite covers concurrency, rollback, ledger arithmetic, audit rows and the leak checks that HTTP cannot express. Folder 07 says explicitly which parts of the wallet it cannot reach.

## ⚠ Everything 429s?

A full run is 71 requests and the global limiter allows 100 per minute per IP, so **two runs inside a minute trip it** — and the *tighter* budget is now `auth:create` (register + guest + claim), 10 per minute, of which one run spends 8. Folder 07 is therefore the first place a too-soon rerun fails; see its description. Wait a minute, or set `RATE_LIMIT_MAX=1000` in `backend/.env` while API testing. `/health` and `/ready` are exempt from the limiter, so they keep passing while everything else fails — which is itself the tell.

## ⚠ Everything 404s?

Then something is listening on that port and it is **not this backend**. Run the first request in folder `00 Health`: it fails with an explicit message when the responder sends `X-Powered-By` or HTML, because this API disables that header and always answers JSON. A stray `node`/Express process on :3000 will 404 every path here and look exactly like a broken collection.

On Windows: `Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 3000 -State Listen` names the owner, `Stop-Process -Id <pid>` frees it. `backend/.env` sets `PORT`, and note the frontend's Vite proxy targets :3000 — so freeing 3000 is better than moving the API.

## Three things to know

**No `Authorization` header anywhere.** Identity travels in httpOnly cookies (`07` §5.3), and Postman's cookie jar holds them automatically. Nothing here needs a token pasted in.

**No `X-CSRF-Token` header either.** CSRF protection demands the double-submit token only from requests carrying an `Origin` or `Referer` — i.e. from browsers, the only clients with an ambient cookie jar to ride. Postman sends neither, so it is exempt by construction, not by a dev-only switch. If you add an `Origin` header by hand, you must also send `X-CSRF-Token` matching the `csrf` cookie, or you will get 403 `ORIGIN_MISMATCH`.

**A logged-in user masks a guest.** `authenticate` resolves the access cookie *before* the guest cookie, so with both in the jar you are always the user. Folder `06` clears the jar before the guest flow and logs back in afterwards — don't reorder those requests.

## Coverage

| Folder | Sessions | Routes |
|---|---|---|
| 00 Health | S10 | `/health`, `/ready`, both mount points |
| 01 Auth | S13–S14 | register, login, me, refresh |
| 02 Games | S17 | `/games`, `/games/:slug` |
| 03 Tables | S18 | create, mine, detail, patch |
| 04 Invites | S19 | mint, list, resolve (public), revoke |
| 05 Seats | S20 | claim, bot, release (dev-only `/_probe`) |
| 06 Guest | S16, S18 | `/auth/guest`, the table binding |
| 07 Wallet & the claim | S21–S22 | `/auth/guest/claim`, `/_probe/wallet` — journey J2 |
| 08 Boundary | S12 | validation, coercion, unknown keys, 404s |
| 09 Teardown | S13, S18–S19 | close table, logout |

Coin *amounts* are out of reach here: nothing is earnable over HTTP until S36 settles a match, so folder 07 asserts the claim's structure and leaves the ledger arithmetic to `tests/{unit,integration}/wallet/`. `backend/scripts/dev-credit.ts` grants coins by hand when you want to watch 900 provisional become 500 vested.

Phase F moves live table traffic to Socket.IO, which Postman cannot exercise — `backend/scripts/dev-socket.ts` (S23) is the tool for that.

item.name: 07 Wallet & the claim — journey J2 (S21 + S22)
item.description:
★ The journey the whole product is built to make work: a friend joins with no account, and signs up **without leaving the table** — keeping their seat and their coins, or neither.

The first request clears the cookie jar and the last logs back in as the host, so folder 09 can still tear down. **Do not reorder them.**

**What this folder cannot show:** coin *amounts*. There is no way to earn a coin over HTTP until S36 settles a match, so every balance here is 0 and `vestedCoins` is 0. The cap arithmetic and the 120→120 / 900→500 vesting cases are asserted in `tests/unit/wallet/` and `tests/integration/wallet/`; to walk them by hand, use `npx tsx scripts/dev-credit.ts --guest-cookie /tmp/g.txt --amount 120` and `backend/requests/wallet.http`.

**What it can assert, and does:** that the `TableMember` row keeps its own **id**. The seat map carries `memberId` (the row id — not an account id, which it deliberately never carries), so this folder captures it before the claim and demands the same value afterwards. That single comparison is the session: an implementation that deleted and re-inserted the row would pass every other assertion here and fail this one.

**Budget note.** `/auth/register`, `/auth/guest` and `/auth/guest/claim` share one rate-limit bucket — `auth:create`, 10 per minute per IP — because each of them mints an account and burns an argon2 hash, and an attacker must not get ten of each. A full collection run spends **8** of those 10 (register, two guest joins in folder 06, one here, four claims), so a second run inside the same minute will 429 in this folder before it 429s anywhere else. That is the tightest budget in the collection now, tighter than the global 100/min. If you add a request here that registers, joins as a guest, or claims, take one out — or accept that the collection needs a full minute between runs.

The i18n-key-in-`fieldErrors` check that used to live here (a claim with a five-character password) was removed for exactly that reason: folder 08 asserts the same contract on a route that costs no budget, and `tests/integration/wallet/guest-claim.test.ts` asserts it on this one.

item.name: 09 Teardown
item.description: Closes the table and ends the session. Run last — everything above needs both.

request.description: 204, and in Studio the row is `CLOSED` with `closedAt` set — **never deleted**. The event log, match results and ledger rows all reference this table, and a cascade would erase the history that pays people. Closing twice is idempotent.
No new join links for a table nobody can join.

Revokes the whole refresh-token family and clears the cookies regardless of what the server found — "log me out" has exactly one acceptable outcome from the browser's side.

This is why the refresh cookie's path is `/api/v1/auth` rather than `/api/v1/auth/refresh`: logout has to *read* it to revoke the family it belongs to.
